headlines.title: 황기연 수은 행장 “ 다음 50년도 수출강국 버팀목될 것 ”
headlines.summary: 한국수출입은행 설립 50주년 기념식 AI·반도체 등 전략산업 금융지원 확대 “수출 1조달러 시대 정책금융 중심축” [한국수출입은행 제공] 황기연(사진) 수출입은행장이 은행 설립 50주년을 맞아 “다음 50년에도 대한민국 경제의 든든한 버팀목이 되겠다”고 강조했다.

headlines.title: 한국 月수출 1000억달러 첫 돌파 …獨·中·美 이은 4번째 기록
headlines.summary: 반도체 호황 힙입어 6월 1022억달러 수출 22일 관세청에 따르면 이달 1일부터 20일까지 수출은 620억 달러로 지난해 동기 대비 60.4% 증가해 동기간 역대 최대 실적을 기록했다. 같은 기간 수입도 445억달러로 23.2% 늘었으며 무역수지는 175억 달러 흑자를 기록했다. 이날 인천 연수구 인천신항 컨테이너 터미널에 컨테이너가 쌓여 있다.

headlines.title: ‘월1000억弗’ 수출에도 기쁘지 않은 이유…‘ 1500원대 고환율 ’, 디커...
headlines.summary: ■ 수출액 1023억달러 ‘세계 4강’ 6월 전년 동기대비 70.9% 올라 호황지속땐 ‘年 1조달러’ 새역사 반도체도 월 400억달러 첫 돌파 무역 흑자는 300억달러 넘어서 한국의 6월 수출액이 1023억 달러를 기록하면서 ‘월 수출액 1000억 달러 시대’를 열었다.

headlines.title: “ 전고점 1560원 돌파가 분수령 …환율, 중장기로는 완만한 하락”
headlines.summary: 상반기 환율 결산·전문가 하반기 전망 6월 누적 평균 1484.6원…외환위기 맞먹어 전문가 “연말께 떨어질것”…시점은 ‘온도차’ 상반기 평균 원/달러 환율이 외환위기 수준에 맞먹는 1484.6원으로 집계됐다. 이란전쟁에 이어 외국인 국내 주식 순매도, 미국 금리 인상 우려 등 연이은 악재가 원화 가치 하락을 부추긴 결과다.

headlines.title: [Why&Next]"6월 평균 1528원"…연말 환율 ' 1430원 vs 1530원 ', 핵심 변수는
headlines.summary: 월·분기·반기 평균 환율, 외환위기 이후 최고 1일 역시 상승하며 1560원 선 위협 하반기, 강달러·엔화 약세 추이 주목 외국인 리밸런싱·자본유출 기조·심리 등 관건 지난달 원·달러 환율 평균이 1530원에 근접하면서 1998년 외환위기 이후 최고치를 기록했다. 2분기(4~6월) 평균 역시 1500원을 넘어섰다.

headlines.title: "韓경제 올해 4% 성장" 전망 나와… 반도체 호황에 일제히 상향 조정
headlines.summary: 국내외 기관 10여 곳 3%대 전망 반도체 경기가 예상보다 더 강한 호조세를 띠면서 올해 우리나라 경제성장률이 4%에 달할 것이라는 전망이 나왔다. 1일 금융권에 따르면 영국 캐피털 이코노믹스(CE)는 최근 보고서에서 우리나라의 올해 실질 국내총생산(GDP) 성장률 전망치를 4.0%로 제시했다. 이 기관은 지난 2월 1.0%에서 3월 1.6%, 4월 2.

headlines.title: SK, 메가프로젝트 전력 셀프공급 … 10GW 신재생에너지기업 세운다
headlines.summary: 연말 통합법인 ‘홀드코’ 출범 2031년까지 원전 10기 규모 SK가 세계 최대 사모펀드 그룹인 콜버그크래비스로버츠(KKR)와 손잡고 올해 말 국내 최대 규모 신재생에너지 기업을 출범한다.

headlines.title: 반도체만 잔치 , 석화·철강‘신음’… K굴뚝 식어간다
headlines.summary: ■ “이러다간 10년 내 반도체 빼고 중국에 다 넘어가” 여수·포항 상가공실 등 지역경제 휘청 “반도체처럼 챙겨달라” 울상 정부 관계자 ‘차이나 리스크’ 경고 “한국, 중국 보다 나은 건 반도체 뿐” 김성훈·신병남 기자, 포항=박천학·여수=김대우 기자 “지역 전통산업의 근간이 휘청거리는데 경기는 오죽하겠습니까.

headlines.title: 중동 리스크 대응 … 정부, 공급망 선도기업 29곳 추가 지정
headlines.summary: 핵심광물·이차전지·물류 분야 선정…누적 216개사로 확대 공급망안정화기금 우대 지원…대출 한도 확대·금리 혜택 "공급망 핵심기업 지속 발굴…대외 충격 대응 역량 강화" [카비마스=AP/뉴시스] 2026년 1월 7일(현지시간) 베네수엘라 카비마스에 사용되지 않는 원유 펌프잭이 서 있는 모습. 2026.06.02.

headlines.title: “ 이미 예상했던 일 … 규제 상관없이 집 살 것 ”

headlines.title: “ 깎아달라 ” “ 못 내린다 ”… 용인 기흥은 ‘ 줄다리기중 ’

key_headlines.title: Semiconductor Boom Masks Weakness in Traditional Industries
key_headlines.summary: While semiconductor exports surge, traditional industries like petrochemicals and steel are struggling, with concerns that without government support comparable to semiconductor assistance, Korea risks losing non-semiconductor sectors to China within a decade.

key_headlines.title: Term Premium Hits 3-Year High, Pressuring Long-Term Rates and Mortgage Rates
key_headlines.summary: The term premium on 10-year government bonds reached its highest level in 3 years and 7 months due to inflation and fiscal expansion concerns, causing government bond yields to exceed 4% and pushing household mortgage rates to an average of 4.32%.

key_headlines.title: Korea Enters $100 Billion Monthly Export Era with June Surge
key_headlines.summary: June exports reached $102.3 billion, a 70.9% year-on-year increase, marking the first month of $100 billion-plus exports and setting a record high for semiconductor exports at $40 billion monthly.

key_headlines.title: GDP Growth Forecast Revised Upward to 4% on Semiconductor Strength
key_headlines.summary: Multiple domestic and international financial institutions have raised South Korea's 2026 GDP growth forecast to 4%, up from previous 3% projections, driven by stronger-than-expected semiconductor sector performance.

key_headlines.title: Seoul Apartment Prices Continue 72-Week Winning Streak Amid Rental Market Surge
key_headlines.summary: Seoul apartment prices rose 0.30% in the latest week, extending a 72-week consecutive increase, while rental prices including villas have surged to record levels with some areas seeing 25-30% monthly rent increases.

sections.Hot Economy News: South Korea's economy shows a bifurcated growth pattern, with semiconductor exports reaching record $100 billion monthly levels while traditional industries like petrochemicals and steel face significant headwinds. The June export surge of 70.9% year-on-year reflects strong global demand for chips, yet concerns persist about overreliance on semiconductors with limited spillover to other sectors. Multiple economic institutions have raised 2026 GDP growth forecasts to 4%, a significant improvement from earlier 3% projections, though this optimistic outlook depends heavily on sustained semiconductor demand rather than broad-based industrial expansion.
sections.Macro & Fiscal Policy: Korea's June consumer inflation reached 3.2%, the highest in 30 months, driven primarily by agricultural and livestock product price increases of 6.2%, with eggs, beef, and other staples posting double-digit gains. The term premium on 10-year government bonds hit a 3-year and 7-month high of 1.4% amid inflation concerns and fiscal expansion worries, pushing long-term bond yields above 4% and raising household mortgage rates to an average of 4.32%. The government has launched multiple counter-inflation measures including additional egg imports and price monitoring initiatives, targeting to keep inflation within the 3% band despite ongoing pressures from agricultural supply constraints.
sections.Financial Markets: The KOSPI closed down 2.04% at 8,303.41 on July 1st, with Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix declining 5% and 3% respectively despite strong overnight U.S. semiconductor index gains of 3.92%, as foreign investors shifted away from Korean equities due to rising U.S. Treasury yields and stronger dollar exchange rates. The KOSDAQ index gained 1% on its 30th anniversary of trading, highlighting growing divergence between large-cap semiconductor stocks and broader market performance. Market analysts attribute recent gains to concentration in semiconductor stocks rather than broad-based strength, with concerns that foreign capital outflows from the equity market are dampening investor sentiment despite favorable bond market developments.
sections.Industry & Technology: Samsung SDI's solid-state battery is on track for mass production in 2027, with plans to expand applications beyond electric vehicles to humanoid robots and mobile devices, positioning Korea as a leader in next-generation battery technology. The government expanded the K-TechPass program to attract global talent in semiconductors, displays, batteries, AI, robotics, and advanced mobility sectors, with benefits including top-tier visa issuance and settlement support packages. Korean airlines are benefiting from the semiconductor boom as AI infrastructure investments drive demand for server racks, batteries, and high-value cargo, with major carriers reporting strong freight performance despite elevated fuel costs.
sections.Real Estate: Seoul apartment prices extended their 72-week consecutive winning streak with a 0.30% weekly increase, while rental markets across all property types experienced record-breaking growth, with villa rents surging 25-30% in some areas due to severe supply shortages. The Seoul Metropolitan Government approved multiple real estate redevelopment projects including the Heuksuk 9 area with 1,561 units and mixed-use developments in Seun-6-4-1 district featuring 999 apartments and commercial facilities. Newly elected district leaders made housing supply and redevelopment projects their administrative priority, with multiple projects receiving government approval to expand apartment supply through regulatory adjustments to floor-area ratios and non-residential restrictions.
sections.International Economy: The U.S. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Wash reaffirmed commitment to price stability at 2% inflation, cautioning against expectations of prolonged higher inflation, while indicating future rate decisions will be determined at upcoming FOMC meetings rather than signaling specific guidance. Chinese electric vehicle manufacturers like BYD have expanded significantly in European markets, surpassing Japanese competitors with both traditional EV and plug-in hybrid vehicle sales increasing 2.4x year-over-year in major European markets. The U.S. House of Representatives cited Korea's regulatory treatment of Coupang in a report alleging discriminatory practices against American companies and potential violations of recent Korea-U.S. trade agreements, with implications for future tariff negotiations under Section 301 authority.
sections.AI & Economy: Chinese humanoid robot companies attracted over 10 trillion won in venture capital investment during the first half of 2026, driving rapid growth in physical AI applications that combine artificial intelligence with robotic systems. AI development companies including Anthropic and OpenAI are intensifying value-for-money competition to counter price concerns from enterprise customers, particularly responding to competitive pressure from lower-cost Chinese AI solutions like DeepSeek as businesses prioritize cost efficiency over cutting-edge performance. Global central bank leaders warned that AI represents potentially the most significant economic disruption of their lifetimes, with Federal Reserve Chair Wash comparing the current moment to the early internet revolution, noting unpredictable labor market and financial system impacts.
sections.Others: The Bank of Korea governor proposed central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) as a safer alternative to privately-issued stablecoins, suggesting coexistence is possible and advocating for trust-based future monetary systems centered on central bank infrastructure. The U.S. House report on Korean regulatory practices toward Coupang has sparked trade concerns, with the Trump administration signaling zero tolerance for excessive fines and regulations against American companies by foreign governments. South Korean startup Obigo launched an AI-powered automotive parts quotation solution automating the import vehicle parts inquiry and internal pricing systems, signaling expanding AI adoption across diverse industry sectors beyond traditional technology companies.
